newsitem.title: USA: Florida international trade up 3.5 pct in first-half '96.
newsitem.headline: Florida international trade up 3.5 pct in first-half '96.

text.p: International trade through Florida totaled $26.9 billion in the first half of 1996, an increase of 3.5 percent or $900 million over the same period last year, Enterprise Florida said Wednesday.

If the current pace continues, the 1996 trade total would exceed last year's record $52 billion by nearly $2 billion, according to Enterprise Florida, the public-private partnership that took over some duties of the defunct state commerce department.
The data represent all goods shipped through Florida airports and seaports.
Exports led the growth, rising 4.9 percent to $15.2 billion for the period. Imports increased by 1.6 percent to $11.7 billion.
Brazil remained Florida's top export market, accounting for more than $2.1 billion or $13.9 percent of all exports. Colombia, Argentina, the Dominican Republic and Venezuela rounded out the top five.
Japan led in exports to Florida, accounting for $2.03 billion or 17.4 percent. It was followed by Germany, Colombia, the Dominican Republic and Venezuela.
Office machine parts and accessories topped the list of exports, followed by fertilizer, passenger vehicles and digital processing and telecommunications equipment.
Passenger vehicles were the biggest import, followed by clothing and flowers.
